short_answer.label: good
short_answer.response: Preserving revenue keeps price times units the same, but preserving contribution keeps price minus variable cost times units the same. Since the variable cost does not fall, contribution per unit drops by the whole price cut, so a much larger volume increase is needed to preserve contribution.

short_answer.label: partial
short_answer.response: Revenue is price times units while contribution subtracts variable costs.

short_answer.label: wrong
short_answer.response: They are the same thing because more sales always make up for a lower price.

short_answer.label: good
short_answer.response: ROAS only compares revenue with ad spend, not profit. The revenue still has to cover the variable costs of the products sold, so a campaign needs a ROAS above the break-even ROAS, which is 1 divided by the contribution margin ratio.

short_answer.label: wrong
short_answer.response: A ROAS above 1 means you earned more than you spent, so it is always profitable.

short_answer.label: good
short_answer.response: Statistical significance means the result would be unlikely if there were truly no effect. Practical significance asks whether the effect is large enough to be worth acting on given the costs.

short_answer.label: partial
short_answer.response: Statistical significance means the result is probably real.

short_answer.label: wrong
short_answer.response: They mean exactly the same thing.

short_answer.label: good
short_answer.response: The number of customers equals visitors multiplied by the conversion rate, so a page with many more visitors can produce more customers even if its conversion rate is lower.

short_answer.label: partial
short_answer.response: The other page might get more traffic.

short_answer.label: wrong
short_answer.response: A higher conversion rate always produces more customers.

short_answer.label: good
short_answer.response: Campaign results depend on uncertain assumptions such as conversion rate, order value and margin, so scenario analysis changes several of them together to show pessimistic, expected and optimistic outcomes.

short_answer.label: wrong
short_answer.response: It removes all uncertainty from the plan.
